Sous Vide is cooking it in water.

So you put your steak in a ziplock bag, then put it in water that is heated and kept at a certain temp , let it sit and bathe in the water for an hour or more and then you fry it. That way the steak is cooked on the inside and all the pan needs to do is sear off the outside.

Heres a good write up on it. Theres quite a lot to think about to get it pergect, but i believe a good steak is worth the effort.

http://www.seriouseats.com/2015/06/food-lab-complete-guide-to-sous-vide-steak.html

Now for heat, what sort of frying pan have you got? Hopefully a cast iron one - look on craigslist or at goodwill stores - a good cast iron pan - you will give to your grandkids it will last that long.

So yeah, you can crank your oven up to full and put the pan in there for a while until its at 250+ or so degrees. Then throw your steak on it for about 2 minutes.. DONT MOVE IT ROUND THE PAN! Let it sit still for that time. It will crust and seperate from the pan, then flip it and give it another 2 minutes - but this time, throw in a big glop of butter - not margarine - BUTTER.

Keep spooning the butter over the top of the steak for the two minutes. Then take it, the steak, off the pan and sit it on a chopping board for at least 5 minutes.. 10 is better, and is also so much harder to weight. So give it at least 5 minutes.

Also, if you need oil for your pan, try and find Avacado Oil - its smoke point is around 260°c. Much higher than olive oil or the like.

Oh and when you get the steak ozt of the pack - dont forget to pat it dry with paper towels and then season it liberally with salt and pepper.

I wish you luck in your Steak Cooking Adventures - learn to cook a steak well, you will get plenty more opportunities to live up to your Sex Machine handle.
